title: System Signals No. 9
summary: Trump declares the Iran deal 'largely negotiated' while U.S. forces strike Iranian mine-laying vessels two days later; Canada seals its first European LNG supply agreement from Ksi Lisims to German state buyer SEFE; western premiers align on infrastructure at Kananaskis while clashing over the referendum; Greer says Canada is in a 'different spot' on tariffs five weeks before CUSMA's review opens; and 112,000 private sector jobs lost year-to-date points to structural contraction in the talent pipeline that no announced project has a mechanism to address.
bullets: Trump says the Iran deal is 'largely negotiated' then U.S. forces strike Iranian mine-layers two days later; Brent rebounds toward $97 after a 10% fall; the 60-day MOU framework exists but the White House and Tehran contradict each other on whether the Strait reopening is agreed.

Canada signs its first European LNG offtake — SEFE of Germany buys 1 Mtpa from Ksi Lisims for up to 20 years; LNG Canada Phase 2 FID momentum builds; western premiers agree on trade corridors at Kananaskis while Eby says Canada cannot reward premiers who threaten to leave with infrastructure.

112,000 private sector jobs lost year-to-date, net hiring intentions turn negative for the first time in 2026, and Alberta's AESO grid queue hits 21.1 GW of data centre demand against a 1,200 MW cap — the major project announcements have no accompanying talent pipeline or grid capacity mechanism.

title: System Signals No. 8
summary: Carney and Smith sign a pipeline implementation agreement committing to a 1-million-barrel-per-day west coast corridor by September 2027; Saudi Aramco's CEO puts a 2027 floor on oil market normalization if Hormuz stays closed past mid-June; April core CPI hits 2.0% for the first time in five years; and a week of Alberta political turbulence — a premature UCP press release, the Centurion Project electoral data scandal, two pro-Canada minister resignations, and a cabinet reshuffle — runs alongside federal airport privatization legislation.
bullets: Carney and Smith sign a pipeline deal — 1 mb/d to Pacific tidewater, September 2027 construction start, $130/tonne carbon price by 2035, conditional on the Oil Sands Alliance CCS project whose goals were quietly revised downward the same week; BC and Coastal First Nations were not at the table.

Aramco CEO Amin Nasser says the oil market will not normalize until 2027 if Hormuz disruption persists past mid-June — 880 million barrels lost to date, tanker fleet 'mixed up,' Petroline rerouting at 7 mb/d not a replacement; the 2027 timeline matches the pipeline's construction window exactly.

April CPI core measures hit 2.0% for the first time in five years; UCP committee passes motion for October 19 separation referendum after premature press release chaos; Centurion Project data scandal links Alberta separatist petition to Michigan Republican operatives 10xVotes; Finance Minister Horner and Hospitals Minister Jones resign; Smith reshuffles cabinet.

title: System Signals No. 7
summary: Trump rejects Iran's peace counteroffer as global oil inventories drain at a record 4 mb/d; an Alberta judge quashes the separation petition on treaty consultation grounds the day before Carney and Smith sign an energy cooperation agreement; and two contested midstream ownership transitions — Shell's LNG Canada auction and Keyera's $5.3B NGL acquisition — reshape who controls Canadian export infrastructure.
bullets: Trump calls Iran's response 'garbage' and declares the ceasefire 'on life support'; IEA reports 12.8 mb/d in supply losses since February with inventories falling at a record pace — and one-third of global fertilizer moves through the same strait, hitting Saskatchewan farmers already squeezed by flooding and diesel up 50%.

Justice Leonard quashes the Alberta separation petition for failing to consult First Nations; Smith appeals the 'anti-democratic' ruling as she and Carney prepare to sign an energy implementation agreement the following day.

Shell auctions up to 30% of LNG Canada to Apollo, Blackstone, or KKR; Keyera closes its contested $5.3B Fort Saskatchewan NGL acquisition over a Competition Bureau challenge; Canada sheds 18,000 jobs in April, placing the Bank of Canada's next move in both directions at once.

title: System Signals No. 6
summary: Trump launches and pauses Operation Project Freedom in 24 hours as a U.S.-Iran peace framework takes shape, sending Brent on a $14 round trip and forcing the Bank of Canada to explicitly flag consecutive rate hikes.
bullets: Project Freedom launched and paused as a U.S.-Iran MOU emerges through Pakistan; Brent swings from $114 to $100.
Governor Macklem tells Parliament consecutive rate hikes are possible if energy inflation spreads beyond oil and gas.
Carney calls a new Alberta pipeline 'more likely than not' — no builder has stepped forward, and 302,000 Albertans have signed a petition to separate.

title: System Signals No. 5
summary: Shell bets $22 billion on Canadian gas the same week the UAE breaks OPEC and Ottawa opens a sovereign wealth fund seeded with borrowed money.
bullets: The UAE exits OPEC after sixty years; Brent hits $111 per barrel.
Shell acquires ARC Resources for $22 billion to anchor LNG Canada's Phase 2 expansion.
Ottawa tables $37.5 billion in new spending, including a sovereign wealth fund seeded with $25 billion in borrowed money.

title: System Signals No. 4
summary: The entry fee, the $20 round trip, and the fuel bill landing on everything from airlines to groceries.
bullets: Washington demands an 'entry fee' before CUSMA talks begin.
Oil makes a $20 round trip in five days; airlines cut capacity and grocers absorb fuel surcharges.
Trans Mountain posts its first full-utilisation month; Alberta tables a 120-day approvals bill.

title: System Signals No. 3
summary: The CN bridge, the Pacific pipeline paradox, and the distance between an energy superpower and its nearest tide water.
bullets: A 57-year-old bridge cuts Trans Mountain tanker departures nearly in half.
The Pacific diversification pipeline remains 18 months from even a formal application.
Carney's majority clears the political uncertainty queue.

title: System Signals No. 2
summary: Hormuz premium, majority government, and the gap between Canada's trade diversification numbers and their structural reality.
bullets: Alberta's oil windfall and its inflationary shadow: Trans Mountain at near-capacity.
Canada's diversification story unravels under the gold adjustment.
Canadian ports outperform US rivals for the first time in a decade.

title: System Signals No. 1
summary: Corridors, state capacity, and how this week's shocks move from infrastructure into daily cost.
bullets: Stronger Alberta export dependence and faster project-state coordination.
Canada's infrastructure response to trade insecurity; Arctic connectivity as sovereignty.
Global energy shocks propagating into logistics and household cost.
